answer: An agent raises influence only after sending a nonce-bound work packet across a verification bridge to a randomly sampled committee of economically independent peers. Each peer re-executes the named slice on its own runtime and publishes a mirror of the intermediate state hash. That hash, bound to a hardware-entropy commitment, becomes a vertex in a public work graph. Identities that share one machine collide on the same vertex and merge to a single stake, with surplus clones slashed. Forging a fresh vertex needs distinct hardware and wall-clock traces, a cost linear in each extra identity.
